title: Wisconsin Reports First Measles Death in 36 Years
subtitle: A tragic loss highlights the dangers of falling vaccination rates across the United States.

summary.en: A young child in Wisconsin has died from measles, marking the state's first such death in over three decades. Health officials confirm that the vast majority of current cases involve people who have not received the vaccine. This event is part of a larger, concerning trend of rising measles infections across the country. Experts warn that vaccination rates have fallen below the level needed to keep communities safe. Public health leaders are now urging families to ensure their children are fully protected.
summary.zh: 威斯康辛州一名幼童因感染麻疹過世，這是該州三十多年來首見的死亡案例。衛生官員證實，目前絕大多數的病例皆為未接種疫苗者。此事件是美國全國麻疹感染率上升這一令人擔憂趨勢的一部分。專家警告，疫苗接種率已低於維持社區安全所需的標準。公共衛生領袖現正呼籲各家庭確保子女獲得完整保護。

paragraphs.en: Health officials in Wisconsin announced on Thursday that a young child has died after catching measles. This is the first time the state has seen a death from this disease in 36 years. The Wisconsin Department of Health Services did not share the exact location of the death or other personal details, noting that they want to protect the privacy of the family during this difficult time. According to MedPage Today, the local coroner confirmed that measles was the cause of death.
paragraphs.zh: 威斯康辛州的衛生官員週四宣布，一名幼童因感染麻疹不幸過世。這是該州三十六年來首度出現死於此疾病的案例。威斯康辛州衛生服務部並未透露死亡地點或其他個人細節，表示希望在如此艱難的時刻保護家屬隱私。根據醫學新聞網站 MedPage Today 報導，當地驗屍官已證實麻疹為死因。

paragraphs.en: Kirsten Johnson, the secretary of the state health department, shared her sadness regarding the news. "My heart is broken for the family," she said. She added that the death of any child is a tragedy, but it feels even worse when the cause is a disease that could have been prevented by a vaccine. A vaccine is a medical treatment that helps the body fight off a specific illness before it can cause harm.
paragraphs.zh: 州衛生部門秘書長克莉絲汀·強森（Kirsten Johnson）對此消息表達了哀悼。她表示：「我的心為這個家庭感到破碎。」她補充說，任何兒童的離世都是一場悲劇，但若死因是本可透過疫苗預防的疾病，則更令人難受。疫苗是一種能幫助人體在特定疾病造成傷害前，先行抵禦該疾病的醫療處置。

paragraphs.en: This tragic event is part of a larger, worrying pattern across the United States. While the country was once able to stop the spread of measles by keeping vaccination rates high, those numbers have dropped in recent years. To prevent outbreaks, experts say that at least 95% of the population must be vaccinated. Currently, many areas have fallen below this goal. As of Thursday, Wisconsin has reported 431 cases of measles. MedPage Today noted that all but three of these cases were in people who had not been vaccinated. Additionally, nine people in the state have required hospital care because of the virus.
paragraphs.zh: 這起悲劇是美國各地令人擔憂的廣泛趨勢之一。儘管美國曾透過維持高疫苗接種率成功阻斷麻疹傳播，但近年來接種率已有所下降。專家指出，為防止疫情爆發，至少需有百分之九十五的人口接種疫苗。目前，許多地區的接種率已低於此目標。截至週四，威斯康辛州已通報四百三十一起麻疹病例。MedPage Today 指出，除了三例之外，其餘病例皆為未接種疫苗者。此外，該州已有九人因感染此病毒而需住院治療。

paragraphs.en: Wisconsin is not the only state facing this challenge. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) — the national agency responsible for protecting public health — has confirmed four measles-related deaths across the country so far this year. However, individual state health departments have reported even higher numbers. For example, health officials in Pennsylvania have already reported five deaths this year and are currently looking into a possible sixth case. These numbers show that the danger is not limited to one part of the country.
paragraphs.zh: 威斯康辛州並非唯一面臨此挑戰的州。負責保護公共衛生的國家機構「疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）」已證實，今年全國累計已有四起與麻疹相關的死亡案例。然而，各州衛生部門通報的數字甚至更高。例如，賓夕法尼亞州的衛生官員今年已通報五起死亡案例，目前正調查第六起可能的死亡病例。這些數據顯示，危險並非僅限於國內的某個地區。

paragraphs.en: This recent death in Wisconsin follows similar reports from other states. Earlier in November, New York also reported its first measles death in three decades. These incidents are occurring as the United States deals with a significant rise in infections nationwide, with over 4,500 cases reported across the country this year. Public health experts have expressed deep concern about these trends, as measles is a highly contagious virus that can lead to serious health problems or even death, especially in young children.
paragraphs.zh: 威斯康辛州這起近期死亡案例，與其他州的類似報告相呼應。十一月初，紐約州也通報了三十年來首起麻疹死亡案例。這些事件發生在美國全國感染人數顯著上升之際，今年全國已通報超過四千五百起病例。公共衛生專家對此趨勢深感憂心，因為麻疹是一種傳染力極強的病毒，可能導致嚴重的健康問題甚至死亡，對幼童而言尤其危險。

paragraphs.en: The situation highlights the importance of maintaining high vaccination coverage. When fewer people get the vaccine, the virus finds it much easier to spread from person to person. Health officials continue to emphasize that the measles vaccine is safe and effective. They are encouraging parents to speak with their doctors to ensure their children are up to date with their shots. By doing so, they hope to stop the spread of the disease and prevent more families from experiencing such a heartbreaking loss in the future.
paragraphs.zh: 此情況凸顯了維持高疫苗接種覆蓋率的重要性。當接種疫苗的人數減少，病毒便更容易在人與人之間傳播。衛生官員持續強調，麻疹疫苗既安全又有效。他們鼓勵家長與醫師諮詢，確保子女的疫苗接種進度皆已更新。透過這些措施，他們希望能遏止疾病傳播，並防止未來有更多家庭經歷如此令人心碎的損失。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To defend oneself against an illness or attacker.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語由動詞 fight 與副詞 off 組成，意思與單純的 fight 不同。文中：A vaccine is a medical treatment that helps the body fight off a specific illness before it can cause harm.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be less than a required or expected amount or level.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡的 fall 不是「跌倒」，而是指數值低於標準。文中：Currently, many areas have fallen below this goal.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To investigate or examine the facts of a situation.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見的 look 是「看」，但加上 into 後變成「調查」。文中：For example, health officials in Pennsylvania have already reported five deaths this year and are currently looking into a possible sixth case.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Having the most recent information or having completed all necessary actions.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指疫苗接種進度已完成最新要求。文中：They are encouraging parents to speak with their doctors to ensure their children are up to date with their shots.

quiz.question: According to the article, how many people in Wisconsin have needed medical treatment in a hospital due to the measles virus?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段結尾處明確指出，威斯康辛州目前已有九人因麻疹病毒而需要住院治療。選項 A 是指未接種疫苗的確診案例中「有接種」的人數，非住院人數；選項 C 是威斯康辛州總確診病例數；選項 D 則是賓州正在調查的潛在死亡案例數，皆非正確資訊。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the recent measles situation in the United States?

options.A: The measles vaccine is no longer effective against new strains of the virus.
options.B: The rise in measles cases is primarily due to a lack of awareness among doctors.
options.C: The decrease in vaccination rates is directly contributing to the current nationwide outbreak.
options.D: States with high vaccination rates are completely immune to the recent measles trend.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第三段提到專家指出麻疹爆發需要至少 95% 的疫苗覆蓋率，而目前美國疫苗接種率下降，導致病毒更容易傳播。選項 A 文章未提及疫苗失效；選項 B 文章強調的是接種率問題而非醫師意識；選項 D 過於絕對，文章雖強調接種重要性，但未表示高接種率地區完全免疫，故 C 為最合理的推論。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, what does the word 'prevented' mean in the context of the sentence: '...a disease that could have been prevented by a vaccine.'?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，prevented 指的是透過疫苗的預防措施，讓疾病根本不會發生。選項 B 錯誤，因為疫苗的作用是在疾病發生前保護身體，而非治療；選項 C 與 D 皆與單字本身的定義無關，無法解釋為何疫苗能減少死亡案例，故 A 是最精確的用法解釋。

quiz.question: What is the primary message the author aims to convey in this article?

options.A: Wisconsin has the highest number of measles cases in the United States.
options.B: The government is failing to protect the privacy of families affected by measles.
options.C: The decline in vaccination coverage is causing a dangerous and preventable rise in measles cases.
options.D: New medical treatments are being developed to combat the recent measles outbreak.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章透過威斯康辛州及全美各地的麻疹案例，強調疫苗接種率下降與疫情擴散之間的關聯，並呼籲大眾重視疫苗接種以預防悲劇。選項 A 錯誤，文章未比較各州排名；選項 B 非文章重點；選項 D 文章主要討論的是現有疫苗的重要性，而非研發新藥，故 C 最能涵蓋全文主旨。
